# Get-EventLogAnomaly

<!-- Generated by tools/Build-Catalog.ps1. Edit the script header, not this file. -->

Windows Event Log Anomaly Parser - detects critical errors and behavioral anomalies across System, Application, and Security logs on local or remote machines.

| | |
|---|---|
| Location | `scripts/windows/server/Get-EventLogAnomaly.ps1` |
| Platform | Windows (Get-WinEvent; remote targets need Remote Event Log Management firewall rules) |
| Permissions | Read access to the target Event Logs; the Security log needs elevation or Event Log Readers membership |
| Safety | Read-only |

## When to use

After an unexpected reboot, crash or slowdown, or as a routine check for repeated errors, bursts and failed logons across servers.

## Description

Parses Windows Event Logs using Get-WinEvent (preferred over Get-EventLog for
performance). Filters critical/error-level events, detects anomaly patterns such as
burst activity, repeated Event IDs, service crashes, and auth failures, then
categorizes and shows results in a console table, with optional CSV and JSON export
to the output folder. A log file is always written to the output folder.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-ComputerName` | String[] | No | One or more target machine names. Defaults to the local machine. Local aliases (the short name, the local FQDN, 'localhost', '.', 127.0.0.1) are treated as the local machine and queried without a remote call. |
| `-HoursBack` | Int32 | No | How many hours back to search. Default is 24. |
| `-Logs` | String[] | No | Which logs to query: System, Application, Security. Default is System + Application. |
| `-EventIDs` | Int32[] | No | Optional array of specific Event IDs to filter on. Leave empty for all critical/error events. |
| `-OutputPath` | String | No | Folder for the log file and any CSV/JSON export. Falls back to $env:TOOLBOX_REPORT_DIR, then prompts. |
| `-CustomerName` | String | No | Optional. Adds a &lt;OutputPath&gt;\&lt;CustomerName&gt; subfolder. |
| `-ExportCsv` | SwitchParameter | No | Switch. Also writes Get-EventLogAnomaly_&lt;timestamp&gt;.csv to the output folder. |
| `-ExportJson` | SwitchParameter | No | Switch. Also writes Get-EventLogAnomaly_&lt;timestamp&gt;.json to the output folder. |
| `-BurstThreshold` | Int32 | No | Number of errors within BurstWindowMinutes that triggers an anomaly flag. Default: 10. |
| `-BurstWindowMinutes` | Int32 | No | Sliding window (minutes) used to detect error bursts. Default: 5. |
| `-IncludeSummary` | SwitchParameter | No | Switch - if present, prints a summary statistics block at the end. |

## Examples

```powershell
# Local machine, last 24 h, show summary
.\Get-EventLogAnomaly.ps1 -IncludeSummary -OutputPath D:\Reports
```

```powershell
# Three remote servers, last 7 days, export CSV
.\Get-EventLogAnomaly.ps1 `
    -ComputerName SRV01,SRV02,SRV03 `
    -HoursBack 168 `
    -Logs System,Application,Security `
    -OutputPath D:\Reports `
    -CustomerName Contoso `
    -ExportCsv `
    -IncludeSummary
```

```powershell
# Focus on specific Event IDs
.\Get-EventLogAnomaly.ps1 -EventIDs 41,6008,7034,1001 -HoursBack 1 -OutputPath D:\Reports
```
